title: Beating Earl Hines and the Christopher Columbus hit
summary: The band outplayed Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace, made Christopher Columbus, and then publishing-driven arrangements led Roy to give notice.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We got there and rehearsed, and things turned out real good. We did the sound... We played a battle of music the first night against Earl Hines. Tore him up, baby. Tore his group up. I'll tell you, it was so bad, that when you get... They had those jitneys in Chicago. When you'd get in the jitney, like I used to get in the jitney to go back up to the Grand Hotel, you'd hear like the cab driver talking to some people, saying, "Yeah, that band from New York, I don't know what kind of horns they got, but they really out-blew Earl Hines last night," you know!

The band was a good band, really, and it stayed good until we came back. You know, we made the hit with "Christopher Columbus." I never did get no singing credits on that, but that was part of my tune, too, you know; because of the brass parts, you know. Another one of the things...heh-heh... I should write a book on the things that

shouldn't have happened to me! But we came back. Everywhere we played was heavy. The crowds were tremendous. But when we came back, Ed Fox... His son was in the publishing business, and we started getting in tunes that he was publishing, to get them on the air. And what they was doing was, they'd have somebody make an arrangement, make the introduction, and play the first melody to establish the melody, then they'd either give me a chorus or Chu a chorus, and then they'd take it on out. And you know, we had a lot of good music in there that I wanted to play, and we stopped playing it, you know. So that turned me into Peck's Bad Boy, and I used to sit on the end, smoke pot or drinking or get off on (?) if I wanted to. So finally I couldn't take it no longer, and I just finally put in my notice.
